answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake that only matures after a history of useful work, like a walnut that only opens after seasons of patience. A public lantern of reputation, built from peer attestations rather than self-claims, makes fake identities costly to light up at scale. And like a reef, the network grows stronger as diverse, independent agents interlock: a single fake node cannot mimic the dense, cross-checked relationships of a real community.
